name: alignment
note: Alignment variants, architecture held fixed. Two have never been run anywhere: session-local referencing (the only published measurement on that axis reports a stale reference costing up to 5.9 points and sometimes leaving alignment worse than none) and shrinkage-regularized references. Riemannian alignment is validated-correct here and reported above Euclidean in the literature, but has never been measured in this harness. THREE COHORTS ON PURPOSE: cho2017 is single-session, so the session-local arm there is a no-op and serves only as an assertion that the code path does not move when there is nothing to move; the experiment itself needs bnci2014_004 (5 sessions) and bnci2014_001 (2), which are where a stale reference can actually cost something. Read euclid_session on cho2017 as a control, never as a result.

arms.name: none
arms.prediction: z-scoring only. Equalizes each electrode's scale and leaves the covariance structure -- which is what differs between people -- untouched.

arms.name: euclid
arms.prediction: the reference alignment; the arm every other row is paired against

arms.name: euclid_session
arms.prediction: THE arm this sweep exists for. On bnci2014_004 (5 sessions) and bnci2014_001 (2), expect a gain: impedance drift, cap placement and gel move the covariance between sessions, so a subject-pooled reference averages over conditions that never co-occur at inference. On cho2017 (1 session) it MUST be identical to `euclid` -- if it is not, the session labels are wrong, and that is the finding.

arms.name: euclid_shrunk
arms.prediction: flat at full data. Shrinkage trades bias for variance, and with a full test set in hand there is little variance to trade against -- its payoff should appear only in the few-trial regimes of sweeps/zeroshot.json.

arms.name: riemann
arms.prediction: small gain over euclid. Covariances live on the SPD manifold where the arithmetic mean is a first-order approximation biased toward high-variance trials; the literature reports RA above EA. Costs ~2.4x EA in preprocessing.

arms.name: euclid_nozscore
arms.prediction: isolates how much of the aligned arm's benefit is the alignment versus the z-score stacked on top of it. Never run separately anywhere.
